round6_research.bug_semantics: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF, CWE-918) in AutoGPT Platform ReadRSSFeedBlock (autogpt_platform/backend/backend/blocks/rss.py): the block fetches a user-supplied rss_url with only a scheme check (http/https); urllib.request.urlopen(url) follows the URL to internal/private targets (metadata endpoints, internal services) with no private-IP/hostname blocking, allowing an attacker to probe/access internal network resources. Fixed in v0.6.34 by switching to the hardened Requests utility (backend/util/request.py) which blocks private/loopback/link-local/metadata networks and validates hostnames.
round6_research.evidence: Class members: {CVE-2025-62615} (singleton confirmed by sha256('CVE-2025-62615\n')==alias-0d3bd8c784475190b98074e6; aliases GHSA-r55v-q5pc-j57f). OSV CVE-2025-62615: 'urllib.request.urlopen is used directly to access the URL, but the input URL is not filtered, which will cause SSRF vulnerability', fixed in autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.34 (OSV git range events give misleading 'fixed' e2a9923f3, which is an unrelated frontend waitlist commit; actual security fix is a6a2f7145 'Merge commit from fork - Replace urllib with Requests in RSS block to prevent SSRF', Bently, 2025-10-22). Vulnerable code introduced at 57a06f708 (2025-10-02): parse_feed rewritten from feedparser.parse(url) to urllib.request.urlopen with only scheme validation + 10MB cap; parent 57a06f708^ still has feedparser.parse(url) (no urlopen). Requests util (backend/util/request.py, first added 4908f4633/2024-11-06, hardened bcaf3241d/2024-11-07 'Patching the SSRF vulnerability in Github/Web Search/Request related blocks (#8531)') blocks private/loopback/ULA/link-local/multicast networks and enforces HOSTNAME_REGEX - applied by a6a2f7145. Introducer 57a06f708 is Claude-Code-authored (message contains 'Generated with Claude Code' and 'Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>' x2, claude[bot]); its rss.py hunk is part of the same AI-authored commit. Fix a6a2f7145 (merge from fork by Bently) has no AI markers; 57a06f708 fix-side note: GHSA-5cqw-g779-9f9x (RSS DoS) also addressed in same commit.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The SSRF-relevant fetch path was first written by commit 57a06f708 'fix(blocks, security): Fixes for various DoS vulnerabilities (#10798)' (Zamil Majdy, 2025-10-02), which replaced feedparser.parse(url) (which itself fetches arbitrary URLs) with an explicit urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=30) guarded only by a scheme check and size limit - no SSRF protection. The commit carries Claude Code authorship markers ('Generated with Claude Code', 'Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>', claude[bot]).
round6_research.reasoning: The advisory names the urlopen-without-filtering fetch as the vulnerability; that exact vulnerable code was written by the Claude-Code-authored commit 57a06f708 (2025-10-02), which is also the direct introducer of the vulnerable urlopen call. The SSRF-capable behavior existed before (feedparser.parse fetches URLs without validation since the 2024 human introducer a00df2509), so this is not a clean AI root cause, but the AI-written code is the flawed bearer of the advisory-named vulnerability and the fix had to replace it. No other AI markers on introducer or fix beyond Claude. Verdict AI_CODE_FLAWED.
round6_research.remaining_gap: Whether the SSRF is attributed to the feedparser-era behavior (2024, human) or the urlopen-era behavior (2025-10, Claude-Code-authored) is not fully determinable from the advisory; the advisory's wording points at the urlopen code path, which is AI-written.
